116: 	eof             bool        // if we encounter a valid EOF in a hard place
117: 	definedSnippets map[string][]Token
118: 	nesting         int
119: 	importGraph     importGraph
120: }

122: func (p *parser) parseAll() ([]ServerBlock, error) {
123: 	var blocks []ServerBlock
124: 
125: 	for p.Next() {
126: 		err := p.parseOne()
127: 		if err != nil {
128: 			return blocks, err
129: 		}
130: 		if len(p.block.Keys) > 0 || len(p.block.Segments) > 0 {
131: 			blocks = append(blocks, p.block)
132: 		}
133: 		if p.nesting > 0 {
134: 			return blocks, p.EOFErr()
135: 		}
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	return blocks, nil
139: }

142: 	p.block = ServerBlock{}

146: func (p *parser) begin() error {
147: 	if len(p.tokens) == 0 {
148: 		return nil
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	err := p.addresses()
152: 	if err != nil {
153: 		return err
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	if p.eof {
157: 		// this happens if the Caddyfile consists of only
158: 		// a line of addresses and nothing else
159: 		return nil
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	if ok, name := p.isNamedRoute(); ok {
163: 		// we just need a dummy leading token to ease parsing later
164: 		nameToken := p.Token()
165: 		nameToken.Text = name
166: 
167: 		// named routes only have one key, the route name
168: 		p.block.Keys = []Token{nameToken}
169: 		p.block.IsNamedRoute = true
170: 
171: 		// get all the tokens from the block, including the braces
172: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(true)
173: 		if err != nil {
174: 			return err
175: 		}
176: 		tokens = append([]Token{nameToken}, tokens...)
177: 		p.block.Segments = []Segment{tokens}
178: 		return nil
179: 	}
180: 
181: 	if ok, name := p.isSnippet(); ok {
182: 		if p.definedSnippets == nil {
183: 			p.definedSnippets = map[string][]Token{}
184: 		}
185: 		if _, found := p.definedSnippets[name]; found {
186: 			return p.Errf("redeclaration of previously declared snippet %s", name)
187: 		}
188: 		// consume all tokens til matched close brace
189: 		tokens, err := p.blockTokens(false)
190: 		if err != nil {
191: 			return err
192: 		}
193: 		// Just as we need to track which file the token comes from, we need to
194: 		// keep track of which snippet the token comes from. This is helpful
195: 		// in tracking import cycles across files/snippets by namespacing them.
196: 		// Without this, we end up with false-positives in cycle-detection.
197: 		for k, v := range tokens {
198: 			v.snippetName = name
199: 			tokens[k] = v
200: 		}
201: 		p.definedSnippets[name] = tokens
202: 		// empty block keys so we don't save this block as a real server.
203: 		p.block.Keys = nil
204: 		return nil
205: 	}
206: 
207: 	return p.blockContents()
208: }

210: func (p *parser) addresses() error {
211: 	var expectingAnother bool
212: 
213: 	for {
214: 		value := p.Val()
215: 		token := p.Token()
216: 
217: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
218: 		if value == "import" && p.isNewLine() {
219: 			err := p.doImport(0)
220: 			if err != nil {
221: 				return err
222: 			}
223: 			continue
224: 		}
225: 
226: 		// Open brace definitely indicates end of addresses
227: 		if value == "{" {
228: 			if expectingAnother {
229: 				return p.Errf("Expected another address but had '%s' - check for extra comma", value)
230: 			}
231: 			// Mark this server block as being defined with braces.
232: 			// This is used to provide a better error message when
233: 			// the user may have tried to define two server blocks
234: 			// without having used braces, which are required in
235: 			// that case.
236: 			p.block.HasBraces = true
237: 			break
238: 		}
239: 
240: 		// Users commonly forget to place a space between the address and the '{'
241: 		if strings.HasSuffix(value, "{") {
242: 			return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot end with a curly brace: '%s' - put a space between the token and the brace", value)
243: 		}
244: 
245: 		if value != "" { // empty token possible if user typed ""
246: 			// Trailing comma indicates another address will follow, which
247: 			// may possibly be on the next line
248: 			if value[len(value)-1] == ',' {
249: 				value = value[:len(value)-1]
250: 				expectingAnother = true
251: 			} else {
252: 				expectingAnother = false // but we may still see another one on this line
253: 			}
254: 
255: 			// If there's a comma here, it's probably because they didn't use a space
256: 			// between their two domains, e.g. "foo.com,bar.com", which would not be
257: 			// parsed as two separate site addresses.
258: 			if strings.Contains(value, ",") {
259: 				return p.Errf("Site addresses cannot contain a comma ',': '%s' - put a space after the comma to separate site addresses", value)
260: 			}
261: 
262: 			token.Text = value
263: 			p.block.Keys = append(p.block.Keys, token)
264: 		}
265: 
266: 		// Advance token and possibly break out of loop or return error
267: 		hasNext := p.Next()
268: 		if expectingAnother && !hasNext {
269: 			return p.EOFErr()
270: 		}
271: 		if !hasNext {
272: 			p.eof = true
273: 			break // EOF
274: 		}
275: 		if !expectingAnother && p.isNewLine() {
276: 			break
277: 		}
278: 	}
279: 
280: 	return nil
281: }

283: func (p *parser) blockContents() error {
284: 	errOpenCurlyBrace := p.openCurlyBrace()
285: 	if errOpenCurlyBrace != nil {
286: 		// single-server configs don't need curly braces
287: 		p.cursor--
288: 	}
289: 
290: 	err := p.directives()
291: 	if err != nil {
292: 		return err
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	// only look for close curly brace if there was an opening
296: 	if errOpenCurlyBrace == nil {
297: 		err = p.closeCurlyBrace()
298: 		if err != nil {
299: 			return err
300: 		}
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	return nil
304: }

306: // directives parses through all the lines for directives
307: // and it expects the next token to be the first
308: // directive. It goes until EOF or closing curly brace
309: // which ends the server block.
310: func (p *parser) directives() error {
311: 	for p.Next() {
312: 		// end of server block
313: 		if p.Val() == "}" {
314: 			// p.nesting has already been decremented
315: 			break
316: 		}
317: 
318: 		// special case: import directive replaces tokens during parse-time
319: 		if p.Val() == "import" {
320: 			err := p.doImport(1)
321: 			if err != nil {
322: 				return err
323: 			}
324: 			p.cursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
325: 			continue
326: 		}
327: 
328: 		// normal case: parse a directive as a new segment
329: 		// (a "segment" is a line which starts with a directive
330: 		// and which ends at the end of the line or at the end of
331: 		// the block that is opened at the end of the line)
332: 		if err := p.directive(); err != nil {
333: 			return err
334: 		}
335: 	}
336: 
337: 	return nil
338: }

340: // doImport swaps out the import directive and its argument
341: // (a total of 2 tokens) with the tokens in the specified file
342: // or globbing pattern. When the function returns, the cursor
343: // is on the token before where the import directive was. In
344: // other words, call Next() to access the first token that was
345: // imported.
346: func (p *parser) doImport(nesting int) error {
347: 	// syntax checks
348: 	if !p.NextArg() {
349: 		return p.ArgErr()
350: 	}
351: 	importPattern := p.Val()
352: 	if importPattern == "" {
353: 		return p.Err("Import requires a non-empty filepath")
354: 	}
355: 
356: 	// grab remaining args as placeholder replacements
357: 	args := p.RemainingArgs()
358: 
359: 	// set up a replacer for non-variadic args replacement
360: 	repl := makeArgsReplacer(args)
361: 
362: 	// splice out the import directive and its arguments
363: 	// (2 tokens, plus the length of args)
364: 	tokensBefore := p.tokens[:p.cursor-1-len(args)]
365: 	tokensAfter := p.tokens[p.cursor+1:]
366: 	var importedTokens []Token
367: 	var nodes []string
368: 
369: 	// first check snippets. That is a simple, non-recursive replacement
370: 	if p.definedSnippets != nil && p.definedSnippets[importPattern] != nil {
371: 		importedTokens = p.definedSnippets[importPattern]
372: 		if len(importedTokens) > 0 {
373: 			// just grab the first one
374: 			nodes = append(nodes, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", importedTokens[0].File, importedTokens[0].snippetName))
375: 		}
376: 	} else {
377: 		// make path relative to the file of the _token_ being processed rather
378: 		// than current working directory (issue #867) and then use glob to get
379: 		// list of matching filenames
380: 		absFile, err := filepath.Abs(p.Dispenser.File())
381: 		if err != nil {
382: 			return p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", p.Dispenser.File(), err)
383: 		}
384: 
385: 		var matches []string
386: 		var globPattern string
387: 		if !filepath.IsAbs(importPattern) {
388: 			globPattern = filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(absFile), importPattern)
389: 		} else {
390: 			globPattern = importPattern
391: 		}
392: 		if strings.Count(globPattern, "*") > 1 || strings.Count(globPattern, "?") > 1 ||
393: 			(strings.Contains(globPattern, "[") && strings.Contains(globPattern, "]")) {
394: 			// See issue #2096 - a pattern with many glob expansions can hang for too long
395: 			return p.Errf("Glob pattern may only contain one wildcard (*), but has others: %s", globPattern)
396: 		}
397: 		matches, err = filepath.Glob(globPattern)
398: 		if err != nil {
399: 			return p.Errf("Failed to use import pattern %s: %v", importPattern, err)
400: 		}
401: 		if len(matches) == 0 {
402: 			if strings.ContainsAny(globPattern, "*?[]") {
403: 				caddy.Log().Warn("No files matching import glob pattern", zap.String("pattern", importPattern))
404: 			} else {
405: 				return p.Errf("File to import not found: %s", importPattern)
406: 			}
407: 		} else {
408: 			// See issue #5295 - should skip any files that start with a . when iterating over them.
409: 			sep := string(filepath.Separator)
410: 			segGlobPattern := strings.Split(globPattern, sep)
411: 			if strings.HasPrefix(segGlobPattern[len(segGlobPattern)-1], "*") {
412: 				var tmpMatches []string
413: 				for _, m := range matches {
414: 					seg := strings.Split(m, sep)
415: 					if !strings.HasPrefix(seg[len(seg)-1], ".") {
416: 						tmpMatches = append(tmpMatches, m)
417: 					}
418: 				}
419: 				matches = tmpMatches
420: 			}
421: 		}
422: 
423: 		// collect all the imported tokens
424: 		for _, importFile := range matches {
425: 			newTokens, err := p.doSingleImport(importFile)
426: 			if err != nil {
427: 				return err
428: 			}
429: 			importedTokens = append(importedTokens, newTokens...)
430: 		}
431: 		nodes = matches
432: 	}
433: 
434: 	nodeName := p.File()
435: 	if p.Token().snippetName != "" {
436: 		nodeName += fmt.Sprintf(":%s", p.Token().snippetName)
437: 	}
438: 	p.importGraph.addNode(nodeName)
439: 	p.importGraph.addNodes(nodes)
440: 	if err := p.importGraph.addEdges(nodeName, nodes); err != nil {
441: 		p.importGraph.removeNodes(nodes)
442: 		return err
443: 	}
444: 
445: 	// copy the tokens so we don't overwrite p.definedSnippets
446: 	tokensCopy := make([]Token, 0, len(importedTokens))
447: 
448: 	var (
449: 		maybeSnippet   bool
450: 		maybeSnippetId bool
451: 		index          int
452: 	)
453: 
454: 	// run the argument replacer on the tokens
455: 	// golang for range slice return a copy of value
456: 	// similarly, append also copy value
457: 	for i, token := range importedTokens {
458: 		// update the token's imports to refer to import directive filename, line number and snippet name if there is one
459: 		if token.snippetName != "" {
460: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import %s)", p.File(), p.Line(), token.snippetName))
461: 		} else {
462: 			token.imports = append(token.imports, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d (import)", p.File(), p.Line()))
463: 		}
464: 
465: 		// naive way of determine snippets, as snippets definition can only follow name + block
466: 		// format, won't check for nesting correctness or any other error, that's what parser does.
467: 		if !maybeSnippet && nesting == 0 {
468: 			// first of the line
469: 			if i == 0 || isNextOnNewLine(tokensCopy[i-1], token) {
470: 				index = 0
471: 			} else {
472: 				index++
473: 			}
474: 
475: 			if index == 0 && len(token.Text) >= 3 && strings.HasPrefix(token.Text, "(") && strings.HasSuffix(token.Text, ")") {
476: 				maybeSnippetId = true
477: 			}
478: 		}
479: 
480: 		switch token.Text {
481: 		case "{":
482: 			nesting++
483: 			if index == 1 && maybeSnippetId && nesting == 1 {
484: 				maybeSnippet = true
485: 				maybeSnippetId = false
486: 			}
487: 		case "}":
488: 			nesting--
489: 			if nesting == 0 && maybeSnippet {
490: 				maybeSnippet = false
491: 			}
492: 		}
493: 
494: 		if maybeSnippet {
495: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
496: 			continue
497: 		}
498: 
499: 		foundVariadic, startIndex, endIndex := parseVariadic(token, len(args))
500: 		if foundVariadic {
501: 			for _, arg := range args[startIndex:endIndex] {
502: 				token.Text = arg
503: 				tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
504: 			}
505: 		} else {
506: 			token.Text = repl.ReplaceKnown(token.Text, "")
507: 			tokensCopy = append(tokensCopy, token)
508: 		}
509: 	}
510: 
511: 	// splice the imported tokens in the place of the import statement
512: 	// and rewind cursor so Next() will land on first imported token
513: 	p.tokens = append(tokensBefore, append(tokensCopy, tokensAfter...)...)
514: 	p.cursor -= len(args) + 1
515: 
516: 	return nil
517: }

519: // doSingleImport lexes the individual file at importFile and returns
520: // its tokens or an error, if any.
521: func (p *parser) doSingleImport(importFile string) ([]Token, error) {
522: 	file, err := os.Open(importFile)
523: 	if err != nil {
524: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
525: 	}
526: 	defer file.Close()
527: 
528: 	if info, err := file.Stat(); err != nil {
529: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: %v", importFile, err)
530: 	} else if info.IsDir() {
531: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not import %s: is a directory", importFile)
532: 	}
533: 
534: 	input, err := io.ReadAll(file)
535: 	if err != nil {
536: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read imported file %s: %v", importFile, err)
537: 	}
538: 
539: 	// only warning in case of empty files
540: 	if len(input) == 0 || len(strings.TrimSpace(string(input))) == 0 {
541: 		caddy.Log().Warn("Import file is empty", zap.String("file", importFile))
542: 		return []Token{}, nil
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	importedTokens, err := allTokens(importFile, input)
546: 	if err != nil {
547: 		return nil, p.Errf("Could not read tokens while importing %s: %v", importFile, err)
548: 	}
549: 
550: 	// Tack the file path onto these tokens so errors show the imported file's name
551: 	// (we use full, absolute path to avoid bugs: issue #1892)
552: 	filename, err := filepath.Abs(importFile)
553: 	if err != nil {
554: 		return nil, p.Errf("Failed to get absolute path of file: %s: %v", importFile, err)
555: 	}
556: 	for i := 0; i < len(importedTokens); i++ {
557: 		importedTokens[i].File = filename
558: 	}
559: 
560: 	return importedTokens, nil
561: }

563: // directive collects tokens until the directive's scope
564: // closes (either end of line or end of curly brace block).
565: // It expects the currently-loaded token to be a directive
566: // (or } that ends a server block). The collected tokens
567: // are loaded into the current server block for later use
568: // by directive setup functions.
569: func (p *parser) directive() error {
570: 	// a segment is a list of tokens associated with this directive
571: 	var segment Segment
572: 
573: 	// the directive itself is appended as a relevant token
574: 	segment = append(segment, p.Token())
575: 
576: 	for p.Next() {
577: 		if p.Val() == "{" {
578: 			p.nesting++
579: 			if !p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
580: 				return p.Err("Unexpected next token after '{' on same line")
581: 			}
582: 			if p.isNewLine() {
583: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{' on a new line; did you mean to place the '{' on the previous line?")
584: 			}
585: 		} else if p.Val() == "{}" {
586: 			if p.isNextOnNewLine() && p.Token().wasQuoted == 0 {
587: 				return p.Err("Unexpected '{}' at end of line")
588: 			}
589: 		} else if p.isNewLine() && p.nesting == 0 {
590: 			p.cursor-- // read too far
591: 			break
592: 		} else if p.Val() == "}" && p.nesting > 0 {
593: 			p.nesting--
594: 		} else if p.Val() == "}" && p.nesting == 0 {
595: 			return p.Err("Unexpected '}' because no matching opening brace")
596: 		} else if p.Val() == "import" && p.isNewLine() {
597: 			if err := p.doImport(1); err != nil {
598: 				return err
599: 			}
600: 			p.cursor-- // cursor is advanced when we continue, so roll back one more
601: 			continue
602: 		}
603: 
604: 		segment = append(segment, p.Token())
605: 	}
606: 
607: 	p.block.Segments = append(p.block.Segments, segment)
608: 
609: 	if p.nesting > 0 {
610: 		return p.EOFErr()
611: 	}
612: 
613: 	return nil
614: }

616: // openCurlyBrace expects the current token to be an
617: // opening curly brace. This acts like an assertion
618: // because it returns an error if the token is not
619: // a opening curly brace. It does NOT advance the token.
620: func (p *parser) openCurlyBrace() error {
621: 	if p.Val() != "{" {
622: 		return p.SyntaxErr("{")
623: 	}
624: 	return nil
625: }

627: // closeCurlyBrace expects the current token to be
628: // a closing curly brace. This acts like an assertion
629: // because it returns an error if the token is not
630: // a closing curly brace. It does NOT advance the token.
631: func (p *parser) closeCurlyBrace() error {
632: 	if p.Val() != "}" {
633: 		return p.SyntaxErr("}")
634: 	}
635: 	return nil
636: }

638: func (p *parser) isNamedRoute() (bool, string) {
639: 	keys := p.block.Keys
640: 	// A named route block is a single key with parens, prefixed with &.
641: 	if len(keys) == 1 && strings.HasPrefix(keys[0].Text, "&(") && strings.HasSuffix(keys[0].Text, ")") {
642: 		return true, strings.TrimSuffix(keys[0].Text[2:], ")")
643: 	}
644: 	return false, ""
645: }

647: func (p *parser) isSnippet() (bool, string) {
648: 	keys := p.block.Keys
649: 	// A snippet block is a single key with parens. Nothing else qualifies.
650: 	if len(keys) == 1 && strings.HasPrefix(keys[0].Text, "(") && strings.HasSuffix(keys[0].Text, ")") {
651: 		return true, strings.TrimSuffix(keys[0].Text[1:], ")")
652: 	}
653: 	return false, ""
654: }

656: // read and store everything in a block for later replay.
657: func (p *parser) blockTokens(retainCurlies bool) ([]Token, error) {
658: 	// block must have curlies.
659: 	err := p.openCurlyBrace()
660: 	if err != nil {
661: 		return nil, err
662: 	}
663: 	nesting := 1 // count our own nesting
664: 	tokens := []Token{}
665: 	if retainCurlies {
666: 		tokens = append(tokens, p.Token())
667: 	}
668: 	for p.Next() {
669: 		if p.Val() == "}" {
670: 			nesting--
671: 			if nesting == 0 {
672: 				if retainCurlies {
673: 					tokens = append(tokens, p.Token())
674: 				}
675: 				break
676: 			}
677: 		}
678: 		if p.Val() == "{" {
679: 			nesting++
680: 		}
681: 		tokens = append(tokens, p.tokens[p.cursor])
682: 	}
683: 	// make sure we're matched up
684: 	if nesting != 0 {
685: 		return nil, p.SyntaxErr("}")
686: 	}
687: 	return tokens, nil
688: }

720: // Segment is a list of tokens which begins with a directive
721: // and ends at the end of the directive (either at the end of
722: // the line, or at the end of a block it opens).
723: type Segment []Token

725: // Directive returns the directive name for the segment.
726: // The directive name is the text of the first token.
727: func (s Segment) Directive() string {
728: 	if len(s) > 0 {

When a named matcher definition came from an imported snippet (or any token with an import chain), `Dispenser.NextArg()` → `isNextOnNewLine()` saw mismatched import chains, judged the expression token to be "on a new line", and returned `ArgErr()` — the exact error `wrong argument count or unexpected line ending after 'expression'`. The same synthetic-token dispenser also failed for heredoc tokens in those contexts.

**Fix:** Replaced the fragile synthetic-token dispenser with direct construction of the `MatchExpression` from the quoted token's already-unquoted `Text` (works uniformly for `"..."`, backticks, and heredocs), setting `Name` to the matcher label — producing identical JSON to the previously working cases.

**Validation:**
- `TestCaddyfileAdapt/expression_quotes` (which reproduced the exact error) now passes
- Full `TestCaddyfileAdapt` suite, `caddyconfig/caddyfile`, and `caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile` all pass
- Manually verified heredoc and backtick CEL matchers, including inside snippets, nested routes, block form, and `not` expressions
